The check-up01/06

Nose to tail, in six stops.

  1. Nosenose
  2. Eyes & earsears
  3. Heartheart
  4. Bellybelly
  5. Pawspaws
  6. Tailtail

01 · Nose

We start where they start: the snoot.

Same-day diagnostics in the building, so a wet nose or a dry one gets an answer before you get home.

  • Bloods back in 40 minutes
  • Digital X-ray and ultrasound
  • Dental scale and polish

02 · Eyes & ears

Then a good look, and a good listen.

Itchy ears, weepy eyes and mystery scratching are the most common reasons pets visit. We see them most days.

  • Skin and allergy clinic
  • Ear cytology on the spot
  • Eye pressure checks

03 · Heart

Thirty seconds with a stethoscope says a lot.

Every check-up includes a full listen to heart and lungs, with an ECG on the same visit if anything skips.

  • Wellness exams, nose to tail
  • Same-visit ECG
  • Senior heart screening

04 · Belly

A gentle press on the belly. Mostly giggles.

Weight, diet and digestion, worked out with you rather than handed down. Our nurses run a free weigh-in club.

  • Nutrition plans
  • Free monthly weigh-ins
  • Worming and flea care

05 · Paws

Paws, pads, claws and the joints above them.

Two theatres on site for everything from a torn dewclaw to cruciate repair, with the same vet before and after.

  • Soft-tissue and orthopaedic surgery
  • Claw trims, no appointment
  • Hydrotherapy referrals

06 · Tail

And it ends the way every visit should: wagging.

A written plan in your inbox before you reach the car, and a nurse who calls two days later to see how it is going.

  • Written plan, same day
  • Two-day follow-up call
  • Vaccine reminders that actually remind
123456

Nose · damp, cool, very nosy

Who we see

Four legs, two legs, no legs. Mostly four.

Every vet here sees every kind of patient, and each species gets the room, the hours and the handling it actually needs.

Long ones, loud ones, the ones who hide behind your legs.

A separate dog entrance and waiting room, lick mats at every exam, and floor-level checks for anyone who won't hop up.

3,4123,412dogs seen this year

  • Annual check-ups
  • Lumps and bumps
  • Eaten something silly
  • Cruciate repair

Cat-only hours, because cats have opinions.

Tuesday and Thursday mornings are cats only: no barking, synthetic calming pheromones in every room, and carriers set down on raised shelves.

2,1862,186cats seen this year

  • Kidney screening
  • Dental cleans
  • Overgrooming
  • Thyroid checks

Rabbit-savvy vets, not dog vets who've read the leaflet.

Teeth, tummies and the quiet signs rabbits hide well. We keep hay and greens in every room and never fast a bunny before surgery.

694694rabbits seen this year

  • Dental burring
  • Gut stasis care
  • Neutering
  • Myxo and RHD vaccines

Guinea pigs to bearded dragons, with the right lamps on.

Dr Arai runs our exotics clinic with heated exam rooms, UV-correct lighting and scales that weigh to a tenth of a gram.

418418small & scaly seen this year

  • Shell and skin checks
  • Husbandry reviews
  • Egg binding
  • Beak and nail trims

Your visit

Four steps, nose to tail-wag.

The fear-free routine every patient gets, from the door to the car park.

  1. visit-door
    01

    Two doors, two waiting rooms

    Dogs on the left, cats and small pets on the right. No staring contests before anyone is seen.

  2. visit-treats
    02

    Treats before needles

    Five minutes to sniff the room, a lick mat or a dish of greens, and only then the stethoscope.

  3. visit-floor
    03

    The check, on their level

    Big dogs on a padded floor mat, cats in the bottom of their carrier. Nose to tail, out loud, so you hear it too.

  4. visit-walkout
    04

    Out the door with a plan

    You see the price before we start, and the written plan lands in your inbox before you reach the car.

  • Price before we start
  • No upsell on food
  • Same vet for follow-ups
  • Home visits for the last goodbye
